L01 confirms that informational posts about workflow decisions end with a practical observation or next-step note, not a meeting invitation. This applies directly: the post explains contact decay as a workflow decision but closes with a diagnostic question or concrete action the owner can take alone, preserving the no-CTA boundary."}], "steps": [{"step_id": "P01", "instruction": "Define contact decay as a hidden operational cost in small-business workflows. Explain that contacts—email addresses, phone numbers, customer records—decay (become outdated or lost) silently when manual contact work is neglected, and that this decay masks the real time cost of the workflow. Link this to the owner's decision: whether to continue manual contact management, hire help, or automate.", "requirement_ids": ["R01"], "lesson_ids": [], "evidence_ids": ["C01", "S01"]}, {"step_id": "P02", "instruction": "Give one concrete example of contact decay in a small-business workflow (e.g., a 1–10-person D2C shop where customers ask the same questions repeatedly, leads sit unanswered, or old email lists go stale). Show how the owner cannot measure decay without a baseline check.", "requirement_ids": ["R01"], "lesson_ids": [], "evidence_ids": ["C01", "S01"]}, {"step_id": "P03", "instruction": "Translate the abstract topic into a bounded workflow decision: the owner chooses between three paths—continue manual work and accept decay, hire for contact management, or invest in a repeatable workflow (documentation, automation, or both). State that this is the decision frame, not a recommendation.", "requirement_ids": ["R01"], "lesson_ids": [], "evidence_ids": ["C01", "C02", "S01"]}, {"step_id": "P04", "instruction": "Explain one diagnostic threshold: ask the owner how many hours per week go to repeated, predictable contact work (questions, data entry, follow-up). This number reveals whether the workflow is automatable and whether the cost of decay justifies an investment.", "requirement_ids": ["R02"], "lesson_ids": [], "evidence_ids": ["C01", "C02", "S01"]}, {"step_id": "P05", "instruction": "Outline one practical next step: the owner audits their contact workflow for one week (or reviews the last week's records) to count repeated questions, stale leads, or lost data. This is a diagnostic fact, not a paid service, and it reveals the real decay cost.", "requirement_ids": ["R02"], "lesson_ids": [], "evidence_ids": ["C02", "S01"]}, {"step_id": "P06", "instruction": "Close with a plain observation: if the audit shows 5+ hours of repeatable, predictable work, automation may fit; if not, manual or hiring may be the right call. End without a CTA or meeting prompt, following L01 and the task's no-CTA rule.", "requirement_ids": ["R02"], "lesson_ids": ["L01"], "evidence_ids": ["C01", "C02", "C05", "S01"]}], "constraints_to_preserve": [{"constraint_id": "K01", "handling": "No customer names, deployments, outcomes, revenue figures, or savings claims. Use only the persona scenario (6-person D2C example) and self-built demo scope as illustrative context, not customer evidence."}, {"constraint_id": "K02", "handling": "The post discusses workflow decisions and diagnostic steps only; it does not propose money movement, high-risk decisions, or excluded services. Automation suggestion is conditional on audit results and requires owner approval."}, {"constraint_id": "K03", "handling": "Preserve the frozen persona (owner-operator, tried ChatGPT, compares investment with hiring), Bareni identity (employee-free consulting practice), and human-approval boundary (owner decides, not Bareni)."}, {"constraint_id": "K04", "handling": "Use plain English; distinguish the persona scenario and audit exercise from existing Bareni capabilities; state no invented numbers or benchmarks; treat contact decay as a concept, not an observed customer problem."}, {"constraint_id": "L01", "handling": "Omit CTA. End with a practical diagnostic rule (if 5+ hours, automation may fit) or next-step observation (run a one-week audit) instead of a booking prompt."}]}
